clue.text: I would come in to bowl over, but I've lost my partner

indicators.note: come in to tells us one piece enters the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: to bowl someone over is to wow them
I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A cricketer bemoans that, just as they came on to bowl, their batting partner was out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come in to' signals the insertion. The cricket words bowl and partner set up a match; in fact the definition is a bereaved speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband has died has lost her spouse, so she is a widow.

clue.text: Bird soars above trees shattered in battle

indicators.note: above places the first piece over the second in a down answer
soars means rises, so in a down answer the word reads upwards

parts.note: the crow is a common black bird

indicators.note: shattered means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird flies up over trees wrecked in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soars' turns CROW up into WORC; 'above' sets it over ESTER, the anagram of TREES that 'shattered' signals. The Battle of WORCESTER (1651) ended the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1651 Civil War clash at the English cathedral city bears its name, the last such battle.

clue.text: Object reserved finally disposed of

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is disposed of, that is removed

parts.note: demure means modest and reserved

explanation.surface: A protest about a reserved item that was finally sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally disposed of' removes the last letter, E, from DEMURE. Object looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise objections or hesitate, so it means to object.

clue.text: A wine list amended in the middle

indicators.note: amended means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restaurant's wine list has been revised halfway down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' rearranges the letters of A WINE LIST. 'In the middle' seems to locate the change; it hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrowest part of the torso is the midriff, and the waistline is that middle.

clue.text: November 11th, when Chuzzlewit's embracing parent

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Martin Chuzzlewit is the Dickens hero, so Chuzzlewit's gives Martin's, written without the apostrophe
ma is a familiar word for mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A date in November when a Dickens character hugs his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' signals the container, the parent landing after the hero's first name. Martin Chuzzlewit is a Dickens novel and its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The feast of St Martin falls on 11 November, so Martinmas is that date.

clue.text: Two ways unknown demonstrates humility

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
St is short for street, a way
y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A display of humility in two ways, by an anonymous person.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two pieces: MODE (a manner) and ST (street). Y is an algebra unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is a lack of vanity or self-importance, the same as humility.

clue.text: In The Mirror, quality coverage for whale

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A newspaper offers quality reporting on whales.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden in 'MirROR QUALity'. The Mirror is a British tabloid, which makes the 'quality coverage' wry.
explanation.definitionFit: The rorqual is a baleen whale with throat grooves, such as the blue or fin.

clue.text: I had shown the way to be unemployed

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
led means guided, showed the way

explanation.surface: A former leader complains about leading the way into joblessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unemployed' is read as an adjective: idled workers are those laid off.
explanation.definitionFit: An idled worker or machine is laid off and left inactive, without work.

clue.text: As a beggar, I am unable to support people with old money

indicators.note: to support means to hold up from below, so in a down answer the first part sits under the second

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for people
d stood for the penny in Britain's predecessor currency
am unable gives can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A beggar explains they cannot support people with old-fashioned money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts the 'I am unable' part underneath in a down answer. D was the old British penny, before decimal coinage in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant lives on alms; the word is a formal term for a person who begs.

clue.text: Garment ripped off

definitions.meaning: a long scarf worn over the shoulders, or a priest's vestment
past tense of steal, informally rip off

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a shoulder wrap and the past tense of steal.

clue.text: What's left without a souvenir?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the souvenir word goes round the a

parts.note: a souvenir is a keepsake or reminder

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is left of a trip once there is no souvenir to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: REMINDER goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is the residue or rest, whatever is left over.

clue.text: Tongue or fish with a dash of oregano

parts.note: the ling is a long food fish of the cod family

indicators.note: a dash of means only a little, here the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe query: tongue or fish, seasoned with a pinch of oregano.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongue and fish read like meat choices on a menu, but tongue is the definition, in the sense of a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language or jargon, which is what tongue means here.

clue.text: Feel sorry leader's gone — one showing the white feather

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: to feel sorry is to regret

explanation.surface: A coward regrets their behaviour, showing the white feather.
explanation.walkthrough: To show the white feather is an idiom for cowardice; here it is taken literally, as a bird with white plumes.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a heron with white plumage, so it literally shows white feathers.

clue.text: Quote: "This requires no orthodontic treatment"

definitions.meaning: a short catchy extract quoted in the media
a set of teeth that meet healthily needs no brace, read playfully

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into a healthy (sound) closing of the teeth (bite), which an orthodontist need not fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A short memorable extract from a speech, used in broadcasts, is a quotation of this kind.

clue.text: State touchy about poem

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: touchy means irritable, testy
If is Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A tetchy person complains about a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. The poem is Rudyard Kipling's best-known one, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something formally, as a witness does, is to declare it under oath.

clue.text: Sitting — try and see if it's been altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suggests sitting down to try and see whether things have changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges the letters of TRY AND SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedentary job or life involves long periods spent seated, sitting.

clue.text: One who is slow to pull girl back

indicators.note: back tells us the run of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to pull is to drag
gal is informal for a girl

explanation.surface: A sluggish person is told to pull a girl back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run of pull plus girl around, so 'to pull girl' reads in the opposite direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is a straggler, someone who falls behind the rest.

clue.text: State investigator ill-advised to intrude

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
tec is short for detective
a rash act is reckless, ill-advised

explanation.surface: A government investigator makes an unwise attempt to intrude.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like the noun for a nation; it is GA, Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to turn up at a party uninvited, which is to intrude.

clue.text: Refuse to believe record colour it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that a record was really painted that colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Record and colour seem to be about painting a disc; they are DISC and RED, with IT as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to doubt it or reject it as untrue.

clue.text: Socialist leader — one showing untypical shock?

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist or communist
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A left-wing leader gives the public an unexpected shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock here is a mass of hair, not a fright; red hair is uncommon, hence 'untypical'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with ginger or auburn hair has an unusual colour of mop, a rare shock of hair.

clue.text: Go down and see scholar displaying his achievement

parts.note: to dip is to drop or go down
lo is an old word meaning look or see
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A graduate goes down to see a scholar showing off his qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: LO (behold) and MA (Master of Arts) are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate awarded for completing a course is a scholar's earned qualification.

clue.text: Storytelling enthrals child that's an understatement

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: storytelling in the sense of fibbing, telling lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A tale captivates a youngster, though that is putting it mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthrals' signals the container. Storytelling suggests narrative, but it means telling fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: This figure of speech is ironic understatement, as in 'not bad' for excellent.

clue.text: Gallery rearranged, to a great extent

indicators.note: rearranged tells us the letters of the word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An art gallery has been largely reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' shuffles the letters of GALLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Largely means mostly or in the main, to a great degree.

clue.text: Sapper and irregular may be abrasive

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military engineer and an irregular soldier can be abrasive company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' asks for the letters of SAPPER AND to be rearranged. Sapper and irregular look like soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass-paper coated with grit is an abrasive, used to smooth wood.

clue.text: Seat that has gone to the right until now

parts.note: a sofa is a long upholstered seat

explanation.surface: A settee has been moved to the right side of the room for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has gone to the' tells us R follows SOFA.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to this point, the same as until now.

clue.text: Beautiful girl left in danger

parts.note: a peri is a beautiful fairy in Persian myth

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman is left in a perilous spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A PERI is a beautiful spirit of Persian legend, a staple of older crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril means serious risk or jeopardy, the same as danger.

clue.text: Provide for extremes of trouble in vehicle

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone provides for a breakdown, with the extremes of trouble in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes the first and last letters of 'trouble', and 'in' puts them inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food or what is wanted, to provide for someone.

clue.text: The language of soldiers joining very small unit

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
a mil is a thousandth of an inch, a tiny unit

explanation.surface: Soldiers joining a tiny regiment learn its language.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British army's part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is the tongue of southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Natural ability to be flashy, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is said aloud, a sound-alike

parts.note: to flare is to blaze or flash, so to be flashy is to flare

explanation.surface: A gift for showing off, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' tells us FLARE, which 'to be flashy' gives, is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude or talent is a knack, and that is flair.

clue.text: Welcoming competition, ready to explode

parts.note: an open is a competition anyone may enter, as in golf
a bomb that is armed is primed to go off

explanation.surface: A friendly contest turns tense, with everyone ready to explode.
explanation.walkthrough: An OPEN is a tournament that is open to all, like the British Open in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeting someone with arms wide signals a warm reception, so the phrase means welcoming.

clue.text: Sailors in two shades of blue

parts.note: royal blue is a vivid bright blue
navy blue is a very dark blue

explanation.surface: Seamen dressed in two different blues.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives both halves: royal blue, then navy blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's naval force is made up of seamen, so it stands for sailors collectively.

clue.text: Composer ultimately loth to sell his output

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so take the closing letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A composer is ultimately reluctant to sell his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' looks as if it qualifies loth, but it asks for the last letters of all five words after it. Gustav HOLST wrote The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English writer of music best known for The Planets.
